subtopics.name: The role and impact of transnational corporations (TNCs)

parts.problem_md: Assess the extent to which TNCs bring environmental sustainability to host countries?
parts.solution_md:
Some TNCs contribute to environmental sustainability. **[KU] **Pressure from consumers and governments has encouraged greener practices. **[KU]** For example, H&M runs clothing recycling schemes and trialled rental clothing services to reduce waste. **[KU]** Some car manufacturers invest in electric vehicles, spreading sustainable technologies globally. **[E]**

TNCs may also support conservation projects. **[KU]** For example, some airlines fund carbon offsetting schemes and tree planting. **[KU]** Corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives can raise awareness and provide funding for environmental protection. **[E]**

However, many TNCs increase environmental damage. **[E]** Factories in LICs often produce high levels of air and water pollution where regulations are weaker. **[KU]** Resource extraction by mining and oil companies leads to deforestation, soil erosion, and biodiversity loss. **[KU]** Global supply chains increase carbon emissions due to shipping and aviation. **[E]** For example, fast fashion creates vast textile waste and contributes to microplastic pollution. **[KU]**

Overall, while some TNCs adopt sustainable practices, most prioritise profits over the environment. **[E]** Their scale means they can make major improvements if they commit to sustainability, but evidence suggests most impacts are still negative. **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word '**assess'** means that the answer needs to include judgement about whether TNCs can bring environmental stability to a country it is based in.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 **[KU]** + AO3 **[E]**
> 
> - A top-level 3 answer [7 marks] will be a clear, detailed explanation with named examples and a balanced assessment.
> 
>   - It should show knowledge and understanding **[KU]** of positive and negative environmental roles of TNCs, using examples to support the discussion.
>   - Evaluate (judge) **[E]** the positive and negative impacts.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The above answer is one way to respond to this question, depending on the case study/example used.
> 
> **Common errors**
> 
> - Common places where students lose marks include:
> 
>   - Assuming all TNCs are 'bad' or all 'good'.
>   - Forgetting to use examples of sustainable initiatives.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Always **weigh positives against negatives** to reach Level 3 in 'the extent to which' questions.

parts.problem_md: Assess the extent to which globalisation reduces the development gap.
parts.solution_md:
Globalisation can help reduce the development gap because it brings investment, trade, and opportunities to LICs and MICs.** [KU]** For example, TNCs set up in India and China created millions of jobs in factories and call centres. **[KU]** These jobs provide incomes, improve skills, and reduce poverty. **[E]** Globalisation also increases access to foreign markets. **[KU]** Countries such as Vietnam export manufactured goods to HICs, earning foreign exchange and boosting GDP. **[E]**

In addition, globalisation spreads technologies and ideas. **[KU]** Mobile banking in Kenya allows small businesses to trade more effectively. **[KU]** Remittances from workers abroad also transfer wealth to poorer countries. **[E]**

However, globalisation can widen the gap if its benefits are uneven. **[E]** Many jobs are low-paid, with poor working conditions. **[KU]** Profits often leak back to HICs, leaving host countries with limited long-term gains. **[E]** Global trade rules still favour richer nations, and subsidies in HICs disadvantage farmers in LICs. **[KU]**

Overall, globalisation can reduce the gap, but only when countries have good governance and policies for managing foreign investment. **[E]** Without regulation, it may increase inequality within and between countries. **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word '**assess'** means that the answer needs to include judgement about whether the development gap is reduced because of globalisation.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 **[KU]** + AO3 **[E]**
> 
> - A top-level 3 answer [7 marks] will be a clear, detailed explanation with named examples and a balanced assessment.
> 
>   - It should show knowledge and understanding **[KU]** of globalisation and its link to the development gap
>   - Evaluate (judge) **[E]** strengths and limitations and their impact on understanding the gap.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The above answer is one way to respond to this question. Additional information that could be referenced includes:
> 
> - Fairtrade schemes.
> - China has made significant investments in Africa.
> 
> **Common errors**
> 
> - Common places where students lose marks are saying globalisation helps everyone equally and ignoring negative impacts.

parts.problem_md: Assess how globalisation has changed culture in one named place you have studied.
parts.solution_md:
Dubai is an example of the cultural change caused by globalisation. **[KU]** Around 85–90% of its residents are foreign workers, making it one of the most multicultural cities in the world. **[KU]** English is widely spoken, especially in business and tourism. **[KU]** Global culture is seen in food, fashion, and sport: luxury shopping malls, international restaurants, and global events like the Expo 2020. **[KU]**

Socially, globalisation has made Dubai a cosmopolitan hub. **[E]** Its mix of cultures attracts tourists and investors, strengthening its global image. **[E]** This cultural diversity encourages tolerance and international cooperation. **[KU]**

However, globalisation has weakened traditional Emirati culture. **[E]** Western lifestyles dominate in malls, hotels, and media, while traditional dress, language, and customs are less visible in daily life. **[KU]** Migrant workers often live in separate areas, which can create divisions. **[E] **There are concerns that Emirati identity is being overshadowed by global brands and foreign influences. **[KU]**

Overall, globalisation has transformed Dubai into a vibrant, globally integrated city, but it has also reduced the visibility of local traditions. **[E]** Balancing modernisation with cultural preservation remains a key challenge. **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word '**assess'** means that the answer needs to include judgement about whether globalisation changes a place's culture.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 **[KU]** + AO3 **[E]**
> 
> - A top-level 3 answer [7 marks] will be a clear, detailed explanation with named examples and a balanced assessment.
> 
>   - It should show knowledge and understanding **[KU]** of place-specific information.
>   - Evaluate (judge) **[E]** the positive and negative cultural changes.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The above answer is one way to respond to this question, depending on the case study/example used.

> **Common errors**
>

> 
>   - Only describing tourism instead of cultural change.
>   - Forgetting negatives like the loss of tradition.

> **[exam-tip]**
> In place-based questions, always use **place-specific facts**, not generic statements.

parts.problem_md: Evaluate the role of a named TNC in driving globalisation.
parts.solution_md:
Emirates Airlines has played a major role in driving globalisation. **[KU]** Based in Dubai, it connects the city to over 150 destinations worldwide. **[KU]** This makes Dubai a global hub for tourism, business, and international conferences. **[KU]**

Economically, Emirates supports Dubai’s diversification away from oil. **[KU]** Aviation contributes around 30% of Dubai’s GDP. **[KU]** The airline creates thousands of jobs directly and indirectly through tourism and hospitality. **[E]** It also boosts trade by carrying cargo, linking producers to global markets. **[KU]**

Socially, Emirates brings in millions of visitors each year, spreading ideas, culture, and investment. **[KU]** This has transformed Dubai into a cosmopolitan city with a multicultural workforce. **[E]**

However, there are limitations. **[E] **Many jobs go to immigrant workers, who often face low pay and poor living conditions. **[KU] **Environmental impacts are significant: aviation is a major source of carbon emissions, contributing to global climate change. **[E]** Although Emirates has invested in fuel-efficient aircraft and conservation projects, air travel remains unsustainable. **[KU]**

Overall, Emirates has been central to Dubai’s globalisation by connecting it to the world and supporting economic growth. **[E]** Yet, its social and environmental impacts show that globalisation through aviation brings challenges as well as opportunities. **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word ‘**evaluate’** means that the answer needs to include consideration of the advantages and disadvantages of something and then make a judgement or conclusion based on the evidence.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 **[KU]** + AO3 **[E]**
> 
> - A top-level 3 answer [7 marks] will be a clear, detailed explanation with named examples and a balanced assessment.
> 
>   - It should show knowledge and understanding **[KU]** of economic, social and environmental impacts
>   - Evaluate (judge) **[E]** the strengths and limitations of these impacts.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The above answer is one way to respond to this question, depending on the case study/example used.

parts.problem_md: Using a named example, explain how globalisation has changed employment structures.
parts.solution_md:
Globalisation has made Dubai a tourism, finance, and technology hub. The high demand for foreign skilled and unskilled labour across roles has led to flexible labour policies and open immigration. **[1]**

Dubai’s primary sector of pearling and fishing declined after 1970. **[1]** The secondary sector grew with construction jobs for mega-projects like artificial islands. **[1]** Today, the tertiary sector dominates with tourism, finance, and retail. **[1]** More recently, Dubai has developed quaternary jobs in IT and research as part of Vision 2030. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for knowledge of Dubai’s sector changes, up to 4 marks.
> - 1 mark **[1]** for the explanation of changes linked to globalisation.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer provided above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used will depend on the example used.
> 
> **Common errors**
> 
> - Students commonly lose marks by only describing tourism and neglecting other sectors.

parts.problem_md: Describe two cultural impacts of globalisation.
parts.solution_md:
Globalisation allows people to share ideas, foods, and sports across countries. **[1]** For example, the Olympics bring together hundreds of nations. **[1]**

English has spread as a global language, making communication easier. **[1]** However, Western culture can replace local traditions, reducing cultural diversity. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for identification of cultural changes.
> - 1 mark **[1]** for each valid explanation, either positive or negative.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer provided above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Global festivals.
> - Shared fashion or films.
> - Tourism.

parts.problem_md: Explain **two **reasons why globalisation has increased in recent decades.
parts.solution_md:
Globalisation has increased because transport has become faster and cheaper, such as jet planes and container ships. **[1]** This makes it easier for goods and people to move across the world. **[1]**

Advances in IT and the internet allow instant communication **[1]**, making global trade instantaneous and culture spread faster. **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark **[1]** for each valid reason.
> - 1 mark **[1]** for each valid explanation.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer provided above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Growth of TNCs.
> - Free trade promoted by the WTO.

parts.problem_md:
Study Fig. 6.2, which shows the ten wealthiest transnational corporations (TNCs) in the world in 2006 and 2016.

![Bar charts compare the wealth of top corporations in 2006 and 2016 by sector: energy, finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and technology, in billions of USD.](assets/002-bar-charts-compare-the-wealth-of-top-corporation.png)

*Fig. 6.2*

**Complete **the following passage to describe the changes shown between 2006 and 2016 in Fig. 6.2.

In 2006 half of the wealthiest TNCs were in the ........................ sector, whereas in 2016 most of the TNCs were in the ........................ sector. Only ........................ named TNCs were in the top ten for both 2006 and 2016. The overall wealth of TNCs had ........................ in 2016 and all TNCs earned more than \$USD ........................ billion. A new sector, ........................ , joined the top ten in 2016, but no TNCs in this sector were listed in 2006.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> In 2006 half of the wealthiest TNCs were in the **energy** sector, whereas in 2016 most of the TNCs were in the **technology** sector.
> 
> Only** three** named TNCs were in the top ten for both 2006 and 2016.
> 
> The overall wealth of TNCs had **increased** in 2016 and all TNCs earned more than \$USD **200** (allow tolerance up to 280) billion.
> 
> A new sector, **healthcare**, joined the top ten in 2016 but no TNCs in this sector were listed in 2006.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 5 or 6 correct = 3 marks.
> - 3 or 4 correct = 2 marks.
> - 1 or 2 correct = 1 mark.

parts.problem_md: Describe the features and global links of a named transnational corporation (TNC) that you have studied.
parts.solution_md:
Emirates Airlines is a transnational corporation based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, owned by the Investment Corporation of Dubai. **[KU]**

It provides international passenger and cargo services **[KU]** to over 150 destinations in more than 80 countries across six continents **[KU]**,** **using a fleet of over 260 wide-body aircraft, mainly Airbus A380s and Boeing 777s. **[KU] **

Dubai International Airport acts as its main hub, allowing it to connect flights efficiently between Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas. **[KU] **Aircraft are sourced from manufacturers in the USA and Europe **[KU]**, and jet fuel is supplied from oil-producing nations in the Middle East and beyond. **[KU] **

Global links include code-share agreements with other airlines, worldwide marketing campaigns, and sponsorships such as the FIFA World Cup and Formula 1. **[KU] **Its cargo division, Emirates SkyCargo, transports goods like electronics from East Asia and flowers from Africa to markets worldwide, supporting global trade and tourism. **[KU]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is **'describe',** which means that the answer must state the key points of a topic and provide its characteristics and main features.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 knowledge and understanding **[KU]**
> 
> - A top-level 3 [7 mark] answer will include specific examples that show:
> 
>   - **Knowledge **of features: ownership, base, fleet, hub, services, sourcing of aircraft and fuel.
>   - **Understanding** of global links: partnerships, sponsorships, cargo trade flows, and intercontinental connections.
>   - **Place-specific detail** includes the location of Dubai, the number of destinations, aircraft models, and examples of sponsored events.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Always include **both** features and global links — the question is worth 7 marks, so balance your answer.
> 
> Use **data and named locations** to reach Level 3.
> 
> Mention **how** and **where** Emirates operates, not just **what** it does.
> 
> **Avoid **vague phrases like 'it is 'big'—replace with measurable facts (fleet size, number of countries served).
> 
> **Link points** together to show understanding, e.g., 'By having a hub in Dubai, Emirates can connect flights between Europe and Asia efficiently.'

parts.problem_md:
Major urban areas like Beijing, China, and Mumbai, India, are home to many transnational corporations (TNCs).

Suggest the advantages and disadvantages of these transnational corporations for residents of cities like Beijing and Mumbai.
parts.solution_md:
Transnational corporations (TNCs) have a multiplier effect** **by providing regular employment with a higher wage than people could earn in rural areas.** [1] **Many TNCs teach their employees skills, which they can use to complete different tasks at home or work.** [1] **The government can use the taxes paid by TNCs to build schools, hospitals, care facilities, and housing. ** [1]**

However, many TNCs have faced accusations of exploiting their employees with long hours and low wages, as well as child labour. **[1]  **Some TNCs make decisions elsewhere and do not consider local or national identities. ** [1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - Each valid point is worth 1 mark **[1]**, with  5 marks available.
> - To receive full marks, **both** advantages and disadvantages must be considered; otherwise, there is a maximum of 3 marks.
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer provided above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Investments by TNCs improve infrastructure and accessibility, including roads, electricity, communications, and water supplies.** [1 mark] **
> - TNCs can bring in money/foreign currency/economic development. **[1 mark]**
> - TNCs can influence government decisions that can lead to unsafe working conditions, pollution, and corruption. **[1 mark] **
> - The development of TNCs can cause a loss of tribal lands, hunting grounds, homelands, and farmland. **[1 mark] **
> - Smaller businesses may experience a decrease in profit or face closure. **[1 mark] **
> - Pressure on water/electricity supply. **[1 mark] **
> - Exhaustion/overuse of raw materials. **[1 mark] **
> - Land degradation/land pollution. **[1 mark] **
> - Dependence/loss of work if the company leaves the country.  **[1 mark] **

parts.solution_md:
Globalisation has occurred through improvements in transport, making travel faster **[1]**, which in turn drives even greater technological progress, making travel more accessible and cheaper for people  **[1] **Communication is important for business because the world is becoming more and more dependent on global connections. **[1] **Satellites and fibre optic cables are examples of infrastructure that have made connections even better. **[1]**

> 
> **OR**
>

>

> - Instant/electronic movement of money.

parts.problem_md:
A TNC is considering the following locations for its factory.

Location **A:  **At Newport West, in and around grid square 6748. Figure 1.2  is a photograph of this area.

Location **B: **At Bridgeport, in and around grid square 6244. Figure 1.3  is a photograph of this area.

[Map extract](https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/719016-2027-specimen-paper-survey-map-2.pdf)

![Top image: Newport West port with cranes and cargo ship on a sunny day. Bottom image: Aerial view of Bridgeport with buildings and mountains in the background.](assets/003-top-image-newport-west-port-with-cranes-and-carg.png)

Use evidence from the map extract and Figures 1.2 and 1.3 to identify which location you consider to be the most suitable for the TNC to locate the factory.

Refer to Location **A** and **B **when justifying your decision.
parts.solution_md:
Location chosen:  B,  Bridgeport.

Location B is more suitable for a TNC to build its factory. **[E] **It has flat land, **[KU] **which will make construction easier and cheaper. **[E]** The land also appears cleared, **[KU] **reducing the cost of preparation. **[E] **There is a main road running through grid square 6244 **[KU], **allowing the easy transport of goods and workers. **[E]** A railway line also passes nearby, **[KU] **which is important for importing raw materials or exporting products. **[E]**

Location A is less ideal because it's on hilly land **[KU]**,** **making construction harder and more expensive. **[E] **The area also has more vegetation, **[KU] **which means that clearing land would take more time and money. **[E] **Although there is some road access **[KU]**,** **it is not as direct or developed as in Location B. **[E]**

Furthermore, Location B is closer to Bridgeport **[KU]**, a town that would provide more work, housing, and services for employees. **[E]** The map shows nearby built-up areas **[KU]**, which could help access skilled labour and essential infrastructure, such as power and water supplies. **[E]** Location A is further from towns and more isolated. **[KU]**

In conclusion, Location B has flatter land, better transport links and is nearer to urban services, making it the most suitable option for a TNC factory. **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The question has several command words and each of them must be addressed in the answer.
> 
> - **Use **all the information available to decide which location is the most suitable for a TNC to build a factory.  Think about what a TNC might need when setting up (services, access, skilled and unskilled workers, etc.).
> - **Identify – **clearly name the area you have selected as suitable.
> - **Justify – **support your decision by including  evidence from locations A and B, along with the map extract.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 **[KU]** + AO3 **[E]**
> 
> - A top-level 3** [7 mark] **answer will have a balanced, developed and evidenced answer that demonstrates knowledge and understanding **[KU]** to evaluate (judge or decide) **[E]** where a TNC may locate its factory.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Use specific grid references and visual clues from the photographs and map. Use the photos and map together, not separately.
> 
> Include comparisons: say why one is *better* than the other. Refer to features like roads, slopes, settlements, and vegetation. End with a clear judgement that is backed up with reasons.
A TNC is an organisation that operates in two or more countries. **[1]**
